page.layout: One column of running text, with numbered paragraphs 1, 2 and 3. No marginal notes. Running head at top centre, page number at top right. Signature and catchword at the foot.

main_text.p: dit in conspectum Domini. Ergo, &c. Hic observabimus ordine:

1. αἰτιολογίαν[?]. Non fit injuria peccatoribus, quando nomine Dei accusantur. Immò Dominus atroce injuria afficitur, cū ad scelera hominum Ecclesiae ministri conniuent: & ut illorum gratiam demereantur, Deum offendi non curant.

2. αὔξησιν[?], quę ducitur primùm à specie, videlicet malitia: deinde, à violento motu: neq; enim inter homines humi repere, sed in altū assurgere dicitur, quòd non tantùm in homines & terram, sed etiam in cœlum peccarent Niniuitæ. postremò, à persona Dei, in quem multipliciter deliquerant. Fateor tamen, me non scrupulosè discernere peccatum in cœlum & in Deum: ut etiā D. Beza monet, Luc.15.18.

3. Malitiæ vocabulum quid Latinis significet, hęc Ciceronis dicta ostendunt: Malitia est versuta & fallax nocendi ratio. Item: Virtuti contraria est vitiositas. sic enim malo, quàm malitiam appellare, quam Græci κακίαν[?] vocant. nam malitia certi cuiusdam vitij nomen est. Idem: Prudentiam, ait, malitia imitatur. Hoc postremum Ciceronis dictum ideo ad-

page.notes: Greek words in paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 (αἰτιολογίαν, αὔξησιν, κακίαν) are hard to read in the scan; accents and endings are doubtful, so they are marked [?]. The catchword "scripsi," completes the hyphenated word "ad-" at the end of the last line. Printed spellings such as "dit" and "Luc.15.18." are left as printed; "confpectum" is read as "conspectum" from the long s ligature.
